title: A Review of Financial Performance Studies on Indian Public Sector Undertakings
abstract: Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) occupy a foundational position in India's economic architecture, serving developmental and commercial objectives since the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956. Evaluating their financial performance has accordingly remained a sustained area of academic inquiry across multiple sectors, including steel, oil and gas, engineering, and power. This paper presents a structured review of empirical and conceptual studies that have examined the financial performance of Indian PSUs, drawing on published research in peer-reviewed journals, government reports, and academic books. The review synthesises existing scholarship across six thematic areas: the evolution of financial performance research on PSUs, profitability, liquidity and working capital management, solvency and capital structure, operational efficiency, and sector-wise studies with particular emphasis on the power sector (NTPC Limited, NHPC Limited, Power Grid Corporation of India Limited, and REC Limited) while also covering non-power Maharatna and Navratna PSUs in sectors such as steel, oil and gas, and heavy engineering. Corporate governance and its relationship with financial performance is examined as a cross-cutting theme. The review identifies a predominance of ratio-based, short-period, descriptive studies, highlights persistent research gaps including the absence of longitudinal panel…
venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology

title: MATEMÁTICA FINANCEIRA E MICROCRÉDITO INFORMAL: ANÁLISE DAS PRÁTICAS DE KIXIKILA E ZUNGA NO MUNICÍPIO DA QUIBALA COMO SISTEMAS FINANCEIROS ALTERNATIVOS
abstract: O presente artigo investiga as práticas de kixikila e zungu no município da Quibala, Cuanza-Sul, Angola, como sistemas alternativos de microcrédito e poupança informal, analisando-as através dos instrumentos da Matemática Financeira. O objectivo central é revelar, com rigor matemático, o custo real do crédito informal nestas estruturas comunitárias, comparando-o com as alternativas formais disponíveis, e avaliar o seu papel como mecanismo de inclusão financeira para populações excluídas do sistema bancário convencional. Adoptando uma metodologia mista, foram aplicados questionários a 80 participantes activos em kixikilas e zungu no município e realizadas entrevistas semiestruturadas a 12 organizadoras destes sistemas. Os resultados revelam que, embora as taxas de juro implícitas nestas práticas sejam frequentemente superiores às do crédito bancário formal, com taxas efectivas anuais que variam entre 24% e 144% o acesso facilitado, a ausência de garantias formais e a confiança comunitária tornam estes sistemas racionalmente preferíveis para a maioria dos participantes. O estudo demonstra que a aplicação pedagógica de conceitos de Matemática Financeira, como juro simples, juro composto, taxa efectiva e valor actual, pode transformar estas práticas de ferramentas de vulnerabilidade em instrumentos de empoderamento financeiro. São propostas recomendações para a integração da litera…

title: Effect of Financial Technology on the Financial Performance of Commercial Banks in Nigeria
abstract: The study examined the effect of financial technology on the financial performance of commercial banks in Nigeria from 2009 to 2024. Specifically, it aimed to: assess the effect of Point of Sale (POS) transactions on financial performance; investigate the extent to which mobile banking influences financial performance; determine the effect of internet banking on financial performance; and evaluate the impact of Automated Teller Machines (ATMs) on the financial performance of commercial banks in Nigeria. An ex-post facto research design was adopted for the study. The population comprised twenty-six commercial banks operating in Nigeria, out of which five banks were purposively selected as the sample. Data were obtained from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) Statistical Bulletin (2024) and the annual reports of the sampled banks. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and the Hausman test. The findings from the descriptive statistics revealed that all variables were normally distributed, while the correlation analysis indicated no multicollinearity among the study variables. Results from the estimation technique showed that mobile banking, internet banking, automated teller machines, and point of sale transactions all had significant positive effects on the financial performance of commercial banks in Nigeria. The study concluded that financial…

title: Scanning through space and time: past, present, and future of time-resolved scanning transmission soft x-ray microscopy
abstract: Abstract Time-resolved x-ray microscopy with the pump–probe protocol is one of the most important techniques for the investigation of dynamical processes at the nanoscale, thanks to the possibility of combining nanometric resolution imaging with sub-nanosecond temporal resolutions. Amongst the ensemble of time-resolved x-ray microscopy techniques, time-resolved scanning transmission x-ray microscopy has been, since its inception in 2006, extensively utilized for the study of magneto-dynamical processes. In this review, an overview of the concept and experimental implementations of the pump–probe protocol in time-resolved scanning transmission x-ray microscopy imaging will be presented together with some examples of recent applications of the technique. Possible future developments aimed at meeting the new opportunities and challenges offered by the upgrade of synchrotrons to diffraction limited lightsources will also be discussed.
venue: Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics

title: Patient Capital and Corporate High-Quality Development: Evidence from China
abstract: Based on signaling theory and principal-agent theory, this study takes the new development philosophy as the entry point and systematically examines the impact of patient capital on corporate high-quality development and its underlying mechanisms. The results show that patient capital is significantly positively associated with corporate high-quality development. This conclusion is still supported after a series of robustness checks and endogeneity treatments. Mechanism analysis shows that the capital guidance effect and the governance optimization effect are the two core transmission channels in the relationship between patient capital and corporate high-quality development. External monitoring, represented by analyst coverage and research report coverage, positively moderates the relationship between patient capital and corporate high-quality development. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the positive effect of patient capital is more pronounced in eastern China, non-strategic emerging industries, Little Giant enterprises, and state-owned enterprises. This study not only provides empirical support for guiding various types of capital to establish a long-term value investment philosophy, but also offers decision-making references for enterprises to promote high-quality development strategies within the framework of the new development philosophy.

title: Mass test and treat (MTaT) for malaria prevalence in a moderate transmission setting, a quasi-experimental trial from rural Ghana
abstract: Abstract A principal challenge to reducing malaria transmission is the high prevalence of asymptomatic infections, whereby individuals without clinical symptoms continue to infect mosquitoes and sustain community-level transmission. Mass test and treat (MTaT), which involves screening populations and treating infected individuals, may reduce this hidden human reservoir, but evidence of its effectiveness in moderate transmission settings is limited. We conducted a two-year quasi-experimental study in 11 communities in the Pakro subdistrict of Ghana’s Eastern Region, an area with moderate malaria transmission. Seven communities received the MTaT intervention, while four served as controls. The intervention involved five rounds of MTaT delivered through community case management by trained community health volunteers. Community members were screened using rapid diagnostic tests, and those who tested positive were treated with artemether–lumefantrine. The primary outcome was malaria prevalence measured by rapid diagnostic tests, particularly among children aged 15 years or younger. An intention-to-treat analysis using mixed-effects Poisson regression models was applied. A total of 5,309 individuals participated, with 4,000 from intervention communities and 1,309 from control communities. MTaT coverage increased from 70.6% in March 2020 to 90.7% in March 2022. After adjusting for ba…

Fast Assessment Method for Transmission-Interface TTC Under N−1 Scenarios
abstract: In practical power system operation, equipment maintenance and line outages may cause changes in network topology and power flow redistribution. Therefore, fast assessment of the total transfer capability (TTC) of transmission interfaces under N−1 line-outage scenarios is important for operational adjustment and security control. Existing deep-learning-based TTC assessment methods mainly rely on fixed-order vectorized representations, making it difficult to explicitly preserve network connectivity, variations in branch operating states, and regional power transfer characteristics of different target interfaces. To address these issues, this paper proposes a fast multi-interface TTC assessment method based on an edge-feature-enhanced message passing neural network (MPNN). The power system is represented as a directed graph integrating bus operating states, branch electrical states, line in-service states, and target-interface regional information. A line-status-controlled message passing mechanism is combined with branch electrical edge features, enabling node representations to jointly capture effective network connectivity and branch operating states. An interface-aware readout layer is further designed to aggregate system-wide, sending-area, and receiving-area representations and construct interface-specific graph-level features for TTC regression. Case studies on the IEEE 39…

title: Luminance Saturation in Luminescent Material: From Fundamental Mechanisms to Anti‐Saturation Material Design
abstract: ABSTRACT With the development of laser display technology toward higher brightness and wider color gamut, phosphor conversion materials are prone to luminance saturation under high‐power‐density laser excitation, which severely restricts further improvements in display brightness and device stability. This review summarizes recent progress in understanding the luminance saturation mechanisms of phosphor materials for laser display applications, focusing on the two major aspects of thermal quenching and optical quenching. Thermal quenching mainly involves cross‐relaxation and thermal ionization processes, whereas optical quenching is associated with mechanisms such as excited‐state absorption (ESA), ground‐state depletion (GSD), and energy‐transfer upconversion (ETU). Furthermore, various approaches for enhancing resistance to thermal quenching are systematically discussed, including increasing lattice rigidity, defect levels compensates for the emission loss, cation disordering, and thermal management through inorganic encapsulation strategies. Meanwhile, effective methods for suppressing optical quenching are summarized, such as selecting luminescent centers with short lifetimes, reducing doping concentration, and promoting material single crystallization. Finally, future research directions toward high‐power, highly stable laser‐driven phosphor materials are proposed. This re…

title: Targeting a Moving Threshold: Antigen Density as a Design Constraint for Particulate Drug Delivery in HER2-Low and HER2-Ultralow Breast Cancer—A Narrative Review
abstract: Trastuzumab deruxtecan has made breast tumours with minimal HER2 expression therapeutically actionable, and the descriptors HER2-low and HER2-ultralow now carry regulatory weight. Both were defined by immunohistochemical convention and trial eligibility rather than by calibrated measurement. For a receptor-directed particulate carrier the operative question is not whether HER2 is detectable, but whether enough surface-accessible receptor is present, and suitably distributed, to sustain multivalent attachment, clustering, internalisation and payload transfer. This narrative review asks whether principles established in HER2-overexpressing models, in non-HER2 receptor systems and on synthetic interfaces can defensibly be extrapolated to the HER2-low setting, keeping those evidence classes distinct. Antigen density acts at several stages of the delivery cascade rather than at binding alone, jointly with carrier design and tumour transport. An analytical constraint compounds this: fixed-tissue methods report tissue HER2 abundance but do not selectively quantify the accessible receptor pool a carrier can engage. Within the literature identified, no engagement threshold generalisable across platforms was found; the single measured value belongs to one liposomal system studied in vitro. Lesion-level carrier deposition varied widely in both human imaging datasets identified, which illu…

title: Numerical investigation on the static and modal characterization of functionally graded Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (FG-TPMS) structures: From homogenization to explicit modelling
abstract: This study presents a finite element framework to analyse the static bending, stress-strain fields, and dynamic eigenfrequencies of functionally graded Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (FG-TPMS) beam structures. Effective material properties of a Gyroid unit cell are extracted via micromechanical homogenization and assigned to a macro-scale solid continuum beam following a power-law distribution. To capture localized microstructural responses, an explicit Gyroid TPMS beam modelled in NX-CAD and a hybrid sandwich configuration with dense Alumina face sheets are evaluated. Numerical investigations assess varying power-law indices (p) and beam thicknesses (h) under cantilever and clamped boundary conditions subjected to transverse loading. The eigenfrequency analysis reveals an orthogonal mode pairing phenomenon in square cross-sections, in which adjacent bending modes exhibit nearly identical natural frequencies. The sandwich TPMS beam exhibits superior structural performance, achieving the lowest overall deformation, enhanced global rigidity, and significantly reduced internal stress and strain concentrations compared to the explicit core alone. These results provide useful design guidelines for developing cellular structures with high stiffness and light weight for various modern engineering applications. In particular, the suggested hybrid FG-TPMS sandwich configuration has eno…

title: Rationale, Design, and Baseline Characteristics of the TARGET (Targeted Assessment and Recruitment of Geriatrics for Effective Fall Prevention Treatments) Cohort of Older Adults for Assessing Fall and Fracture Risk: Prospective Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract Background Falls and fractures are a major clinical concern for older adults. International clinical guidelines recommend annual fall risk screening for all adults aged 60 years and older. However, existing falls risk–screening algorithms have shown limited sensitivity and specificity in detecting future falls. Emerging health technologies, including wearable sensors, in-silico finite element models (FEMs), and virtual reality (VR) technology, show promise in enhancing fall and fracture risk assessments by providing more personalized objective data to support targeted primary prevention. However, large-scale longitudinal studies are required to evaluate their predictive accuracy and cost-effectiveness for systematic community–based screening. Objective The TARGET (Targeted Assessment and Recruitment of Geriatrics for Effective Fall Prevention Treatments) study is an ongoing national prospective cohort study in Singapore designed to develop cost-effective and scalable frameworks for the early detection and prevention of falls and fractures using novel health technologies. This paper describes the rationale, design, and baseline characteristics of TARGET, and provides preliminary insights into how these novel technologies perform in discriminating between older adults with and with no history of falls at study baseline. Methods A total of 2291 community-dwelling Singapor…

title: Nurse-Led Supportive Physical and Psychological Therapies versus Orthopedic Specialist-Led Usual Care for Postmenopausal Women with Osteoporosis: A 24-Month Prospective, Non-Randomized Interventional Study with Retrospective Data Analysis (Quasi-Experimental Design)
abstract: Background: Postmenopausal osteoporosis is a progressive skeletal disorder that poses a substantial public health burden due to increased fracture risks. Specialized orthopedic clinics are often structurally constrained by high surgical volumes, limiting their capacity to provide the continuous cognitive reinforcement necessary to maintain long-term medication compliance. Objectives of the study were to evaluate the 24-month clinical utility, behavioral outcomes, and safety profiles of a nurse-led supportive physical and psychological therapy (NT) model compared with traditional orthopedic specialist-led usual care (OU) in postmenopausal women with newly diagnosed primary osteoporosis. Methods: This 24-month quasi-experimental, non-randomized prospective interventional study analyzed registry data from January 2020 to July 2022 at a single center in China. Out of 415 screened postmenopausal women, 381 with complete 24-month data were evaluated (NT cohort: n = 190, receiving monthly theory-based counseling; OU cohort: n = 191, receiving standard quarterly visits). Both groups received standard guideline-directed medical therapy. Primary metrics included the Medication Possession Ratio (MPR), Osteoporosis Self-Efficacy Scale (OSES), and Osteoporosis Health Belief Scale (OHBS). Separate multivariable linear and logistic regression models adjusted for baseline covariates, with a Bo…

title: A Triple-Magnet Passive Gravity Compensator: Sensitivity-Based Design and Experimental Validation
abstract: Abstract Passive magnetic gravity compensation using permanent magnets provides an energy-free solution for counterbalancing gravitational loads; however, the design of such systems typically involves high-dimensional parameter spaces, making conventional optimization methods computationally expensive. This paper proposes a triple-magnet configuration for gravity compensation of linear motion. A simplified design methodology is developed based on sensitivity-guided variable reduction for design optimization, through which the original nine-variable design problem is reduced to a two-stage, one-dimensional search. The proposed method is validated through numerical studies and compared with a full nine-variable genetic algorithm optimization, with results showing that the simplified method achieves an average gravity reduction rate (AGRR) exceeding 93% while reducing computational time by approximately 9-fold. The design is further realized using commercially available magnets and experimentally validated. The proposed approach thus provides a practical concept and efficient framework for the design of passive magnetic gravity compensators for linear motion.

title: Impact of augmented reality on narrative-related outcomes in children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: a within-subject design
abstract: Inroduction Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is commonly associated with impairments in social communication, narrative abilities, and socio-cognitive functioning. This study explored whether augmented reality (AR) could enhance narrative production, comprehension, use of mental state language, and reading-related behaviors in children with ASD. Methods Fifteen children with ASD without intellectual disability participated in a within-subjects design in which they completed story retelling tasks under two counterbalanced conditions: a traditional paper-based format and a tablet-based format. Narrative performance was assessed through measures of microstructure, including productivity, lexical diversity, and syntax, as well as macrostructure indicators such as recall of main ideas. Oral comprehension and reading-oriented behaviors were also examined. Results Results showed that the AR condition significantly improved socio-cognitive and behavioral outcomes. Children produced a higher number of mental state terms and demonstrated greater attention, persistence, and engagement during the tasks. These findings suggest that AR can function as an effective scaffold that facilitates the explicit representation of internal states while increasing attentional involvement. Discussion Consequently, AR technology may represent a promising tool for improving language assessment and fostering …

title: Design and Implementation of a Laravel-Based Hybrid Monitoring and Control System for the Cah Fungi Mushroom House
abstract: Oyster mushroom cultivation requires stable temperature and humidity conditions to maintain a suitable growing-house environment. This study aims to design and develop a Laravel-based hybrid monitoring and control system for the Cah Fungi mushroom growing house by integrating environmental monitoring, device control, and parameter configuration into a single web application. The system uses an ESP32 and DHT22 sensor for data acquisition, MQTT for communication, MySQL for data storage, and Laravel as the central platform for data processing and control logic. Automatic control applies temperature thresholds of 22–28 °C and relative humidity thresholds of 80–90%, while manual control allows users to perform a manual override through the dashboard. The system was developed using the Waterfall method and evaluated using Black Box Testing and response-time measurements. The results show that monitoring, MQTT communication, automatic and manual control, manual override, dynamic configuration, and data visualization operated as designed. The system achieved an average response time of 0.407 seconds, while control parameters could be updated without reflashing the ESP32 firmware. Future development should incorporate CO₂ and light-intensity sensors to provide more comprehensive environmental monitoring.

title: Cocreation of Digital Outcome Measures for Dravet Syndrome: Multistage Co-Design Feasibility Study
abstract: Abstract Background Dravet syndrome is a complex developmental and epileptic encephalopathy characterized by treatment-resistant seizures and multiple comorbidities that significantly affect quality of life. Traditional clinic-based assessments often fail to capture real-world functional abilities and behavioral changes. Objective This study aimed to (1) identify caregiver-prioritized meaningful aspects of health, (2) co-design digital assessment modalities for home use, and (3) generate preliminary usability and implementation insights to inform future clinical research. Methods A multistage patient and public involvement activity was conducted between November 2023 and October 2025 in Spain, in collaboration with a patient advocacy organization and a digital health company. Participants were recruited through the Fundación Síndrome de Dravet using a convenience opt-in sampling approach. The process included a caregiver survey to identify meaningful aspects of health, a design workshop to refine priorities and technology preferences, and a 2-week usability testing of a prototype app, followed by a feedback workshop. Data were analyzed descriptively to inform iterative cocreation; no hypothesis testing was performed. Results Fifty caregivers completed the survey. Neuropsychiatric symptoms (17/48, 35%), independence (16/48, 33%), and social or leisure activities (15/48, 31%) wer…

title: A generic and integrated design framework for multi-configuration morphing wing structure
abstract: Abstract Morphing wing structures represent an outstanding advancement in aerospace technology, enabling enhanced fuel efficiency, improved manoeuvrability, and reduced noise. However, existing approaches, whether traditional mechanical-based structures or topology-optimised compliant structures, exhibit notable limitations in structural universality and deformation capability. This study presents a novel two-dimensional design framework for morphing wing structures based on the compliant mechanism and the topology optimisation method, demonstrating adaptability to diverse two-dimensional airfoil geometries and enabling transformation of multiple target shape configurations. The proposed methodology integrates an enhanced Voronoi-based truss skeleton generation algorithm with a nonlinear force analysis approach, eliminating post-processing requirements for geometric smoothing or boundary adaptation. Furthermore, an optimisation paradigm for control strategy and actuator layout is developed to efficiently achieve the transformation of wing configurations. To validate this framework, a quadruple-airfoil morphing wing prototype was manufactured, numerically modelled and experimentally realised. Comprehensive fluid-structure interaction simulations evaluated structural integrity under operational loads, while functional testing of the physical prototype without skin confirmed defor…

title: When national qualifications travel: Curriculum fairness after the 2024 Pearson Edexcel A‐Level Chinese reform
abstract: Abstract National qualifications do not always stay national. Once offered internationally, a reform designed around one education system may reach students with very different linguistic histories. This article examines that problem through Pearson Edexcel A‐Level Chinese, an England‐regulated subject qualification offered in the UK and internationally. From 2026, candidates will read the listening and reading questions in English and answer them in English. The change responds to evidence that earlier papers disadvantaged students learning Chinese as an additional language. It also changes how every candidate must show Chinese comprehension to receive credit. The study draws on entry statistics, policy and specification documents, and Pearson's sample paper. Ofqual reported approximately 5150 Pearson entries in 2023, while the Joint Council for Qualifications (JCQ) recorded 1449 UK Chinese A‐Level entries across all awarding organisations. The difference gives a conservative estimate of at least 3701 Pearson entries outside the UK, or 71.9% of Pearson's total. Yet public records tell us little about these candidates: where they study, which languages they use, or why they take the qualification. The sample paper asks for little extended English writing, but English remains compulsory. I do not claim that the reform has already caused disadvantage. The narrower argument is tha…

title: Labor Market Effects of Short-Cycle Higher Education Programs: Lessons from Colombia
Plant-based packaged foods as analogues to animal products: market trends and nutritional quality analysis
abstract: Abstract Background In Europe, a range of packaged foods that are based on plants are marketed as analogues to animal food products, yet EU-wide data on their market evolution and nutritional quality remain limited. This study aimed to (1) assess the market shares of these plant-based analogues across the EU; (2) evaluate their macronutrient composition and nutritional quality; and (3) compare that with animal food products. Methods Data were extracted from Euromonitor’s Passport and EuroFIR’s FoodEXplorer databases. Market trends were analysed from 2009 to 2024. Macronutrient composition analysis was performed, and nutritional quality was evaluated using Nutri-Score and Multiple Traffic Light systems; eligibility for EU nutrition claims was determined according to current legislation. Differences between animal products and their plant-based analogues were tested using the Mann–Whitney U test. Results Between 2009 and 2024, the market volume of dairy analogues more than tripled, while that of meat and seafood analogues increased approximately sevenfold. Macronutrient analysis revealed great variability within categories. Protein content varied widely, particularly among analogues to curded dairy products, with many products providing little to no protein. Nutri-Score showed consistent patterns: approximately 50% of meat and seafood analogues scored A or B; dairy drink analogue…

title: Early career effects of entering the labor market during higher education expansion
abstract: Abstract We evaluate the labor market effects of an increasing supply of high-skilled labor, resulting from a higher education expansion at established German universities. Exploiting variation in exposure across regions and cohorts, we estimate early career effects for labor market entrants. We find that high-skilled wages decline initially, particularly in non-graduate jobs, but recover over the first 5 years of experience. For graduate job takers, we even report positive wage effects after 5 years. We explain the dynamics of the effects by the interplay of several mechanisms: immediate supply effects, recovery through regional mobility, and increased productivity of graduate jobs.

title: Effect of the combined use of resin infiltration and bioactive glass on the surface properties of white spot lesions with or without sodium hypochlorite pretreatment: an in vitro study
AI and the clinical blind spot: why psychiatry should be part of the conversation about artificial intelligence and human behaviour
abstract: Summary Artificial intelligence (AI) systems that model human behaviour are built on data humans generate about themselves, yet the assumption that this data is reliable remains largely unexamined. Psychiatry’s evidence base directly challenges it. Self-report is shaped by cognitive distortions, the gap between clinical presentation and underlying experience, and conditions that make accurate self-report impossible. The populations most affected by AI-driven decisions can be the least represented in training data. Clinical expertise in the reliability of human data, which psychiatry holds and practises daily, is largely absent from AI development. This omission is correctable, but psychiatry must enter the conversation.

title: Market Pareidolia: a new categorization of international markets by human age
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to introduce Market Pareidolia, a conceptual and data-driven framework that categorizes foreign markets according to human age stages: adolescence, adulthood and seniority. The framework is designed to support early-stage International Market Selection (IMS) by helping internationally active firms interpret, compare and communicate foreign-market heterogeneity before undertaking more detailed entry-mode, investment and risk analyses. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a conceptual framework combining cognitive psychology with international business strategy. Drawing from human age categorizations, 18 human developmental markers were matched to corresponding international market indices across 175 countries. Using Z-score normalization and Factor Analysis, four main factors and two standalone variables were identified, forming a composite “market age” for each country. The approach integrates quantitative data with conceptual reasoning to create a new typology. Findings The study successfully attributes a corresponding “human age” to 175 countries by aligning market indicators with human developmental markers. This anthropomorphic classification facilitates an intuitive understanding of market maturity stages and helps firms relate to international markets more instinctively. The resulting profiles reflect market stability, adaptab…
venue: Review of International Business and Strategy

title: Service-learning as a pathway to sustainable social development: Social inclusion perceptions of international physical education students
abstract: Contemporary academic curricula for physical education teacher education (PETE) increasingly recognize the importance of social responsibility in higher education and its contribution to sustainable social development. In this context, service-learning (SL) is an approach that connects academic learning with community needs, fosters social inclusion, and supports the development of more inclusive and sustainable social environments. The objectives of this study were: (1) to examine whether SL activities help improve the perception of social inclusion among international PETE students, and (2) to determine whether their prior motor experience influences their participation in and experience of SL activities. The quasi-experiment pilot study with self‑selected groups

title: Experience in Applying Artificial Intelligence in the Customs Service of the Russian Federation
abstract: This article focuses on the practical application of artificial intelligence technologies in the activities of the customs authorities of the Russian Federation. The study includes a comparative analysis of the experience of implementing intelligent solutions in the customs sector. The main trends in the use of AI in the Russian customs service have been identified. Additionally, the article identifies the priority areas for the application of artificial intelligence in the customs sector and provides a comprehensive list of modern technical tools with AI functionality that are used in the routine work processes of the customs authorities. The article also highlights the benefits of using intelligent technologies to improve the performance of the Russian customs authorities. One of the possible areas is the development of domestic information systems with AI functions in order to improve the efficiency of customs control and speed up customs operations.

title: Mind your tone: how swear words in online complaints influence bystander perceptions of airlines and hotels
abstract: Purpose The prevalence of uncivil consumer behavior on social media presents challenges for brands managing publicly visible complaint interactions, where bystanders observe and evaluate responses. While prior research has examined accommodative brand responses and online incivility, few studies have examined how complaint tone shapes bystanders’ perceptions of accommodative responses in publicly visible interactions. Design/methodology/approach Two online scenario experiments were conducted with US consumers, using the airline (N = 679) and hotel (N = 553) industries as contexts. Both studies utilized a 2 × 2 design to test the proposed model. Findings Accommodative responses significantly increased bystanders’ purchase intentions, and this effect was fully mediated by brand attitude. Complaint tone moderated this indirect effect such that the positive impact of accommodative responses was stronger for civil complaints and weaker for uncivil complaints. Practical implications The findings suggest that brand managers should adopt tone-sensitive response strategies when managing public complaints, while platforms and policymakers should support tools and guidelines that reduce online incivility and promote constructive communication environments. Originality/value This study examined accommodative responses, complaint tone, and observing bystanders together in public social medi…

title: A retrospective claims analysis of the association between residential greenness and per capita healthcare costs among fee-for-service Medicare patients
abstract: Abstract Nature amenities in everyday environments have been shown to improve health, which may translate to healthcare cost savings. We examined the association between residential greenness (mean NDVI measured at the census tract level) and healthcare costs in a longitudinal (2008–2015) study of Medicare expenditures among fee-for-service (FFS) clients (ages 65+; n = 275,000) across the US. We used generalized linear models to estimate differences in average annual healthcare costs across levels of residential greenness, adjusting for sociodemographic factors. Average annual claim totals were $957.30 (USD) lower (95% CI: -$1,379.80, -$534.80) for participants living in the most green compared to the least green areas. Sensitivity analyses among long-duration residents showed similar associations. While there are many costs associated with greening neighborhoods, as well as other barriers, these efforts could potentially lead to cost savings in the US on healthcare expenditures.

title: How older consumers perceive AI disclosure in advertising: relatability and trustworthiness across utilitarian and hedonic service contexts
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how older consumers interpret artificial intelligence (AI) disclosure when evaluating the trustworthiness of AI-generated advertising across utilitarian and hedonic service contexts and explores the role of relatability in these evaluations. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative study was conducted using 25 semi-structured interviews with Australian consumers aged 65 years and above. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis with abductive reasoning and gerund-based coding. Findings Findings reveal that advertising trustworthiness is contextually calibrated rather than determined by AI disclosure alone. In utilitarian contexts, disclosure was associated with a transparency–scepticism tension, as greater awareness of AI involvement coincided with stronger expectations for credibility and human presence. In hedonic contexts, disclosure was often less salient but was associated with greater scepticism when AI-generated representations were perceived as unrealistic. Relatability functioned as an interpretive filter, with participants’ evaluations reflecting both social similarity and representational realism in judging whether AI-generated content was credible and relevant. Research limitations/implications The study focuses on older Australian consumers and future research should examine other demographic, cultural and service cont…

title: Digital Accessibility as a Service Design Challenge in Academic Libraries
abstract: Abstract Digital accessibility is an emerging service design challenge for academic libraries as access to information increasingly depends on digital service pathways, including library websites, discovery systems, authentication processes, and public workstations. When these service components are not accessible, libraries risk undermining their core function of enabling independent and equitable access to knowledge. Despite growing digital transformation in higher education, many institutions, particularly in resource-constrained contexts, struggle to integrate accessibility into routine library service design and operations. This study investigates how accessibility barriers develop across academic library service pathways and presents an operational model to support inclusive information access. Using a qualitative case study at an African university library, the research combined a WCAG-aligned evaluation of key digital access points with focus groups involving students with disabilities and interviews with library staff. The findings show that physical, digital, and service-interaction barriers accumulate along the access journey, increasing dependence on mediated assistance and limiting independent use of information resources. The article introduces a practical service design framework that integrates accessibility into routine library operations through a continuous c…

title: Motion control of an aquatic snake robot with actuator failures and environmental uncertainties using neural network super twisting sliding mode control
Social service accessibility and Green Agricultural Development Intensity as pathways to Rural Elderly Welfare: panel evidence from China’s underserved regions
abstract: Background The elderly population in the rural areas of China, defined as 60 years or older, is over 121 million, representing 23.8% of the total rural population. The elderly population is growing rapidly and is characterized by the triple burden of poor access to healthcare, reduced agricultural income, and being digitally excluded. Although numerous national programs to expand social services and promote green agricultural transformation have been developed, the overall impact of these two policy streams on elderly wellbeing remains an untested area. This study aims to examine the independent and combined effects of social service accessibility (SSA) and Green Agricultural Development Intensity (GADI) on Rural Elderly Welfare (REW), while considering livelihood resilience (LR) as the mediating variable and the digital divide index (DDI) as the moderating condition. Both SSA and GADI are operationalized as province-level composite indices of service provision and agricultural development intensity, respectively, rather than as direct measures of individual elderly residents’ service use or farming behavior; this measurement level is made explicit throughout. Methods A panel data set was created, with the data collected at the provincial level and covering 30 provinces in China from 2013 to 2022 ( N = 268). Three province-year cells are missing because Tibet and Hainan entered…

title: Fueling service initiative: how AI assimilation shapes employees' proactive service behavior through AI crafting
abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally reshaping how employees engage in service work. However, few studies have examined how AI assimilation (i.e. the extent to which AI technology is integrated and routinized in work activities and processes) affects employees' proactive behaviors. This study investigates how the breadth and depth of AI assimilation shape proactive service behavior, examines the mediating roles of approach and avoidance AI crafting, and tests job autonomy as a moderator. It further examines whether employees exhibit higher proactive service behavior when these two crafting strategies are used in a more balanced way. Design/methodology/approach Based on Conservation Of Resources (COR) theory, this study uses paired-sample survey data from 234 employee-manager pairs in China's service industry. Stepwise regression, polynomial regression, and response surface analysis are applied to test the hypotheses. Findings The results show that both the depth and breadth of AI assimilation positively influence proactive service behavior. Approach AI crafting mediates both relationships, while avoidance AI crafting only mediates the relationship between the breadth of AI assimilation and proactive service behavior. Employees exhibit the highest level of proactive service behavior when using both crafting strategies in balance, indicating that approach and avo…

title: Too little time, too much to do: how time poverty undermines employees’ proactive service behavior
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine the relationship between time poverty and hotel employees’ proactive service behavior by identifying future self-continuity as a mediator and competitive climate as a moderator. Design/methodology/approach This research uses a multimethod design to test the hypotheses. Study 1 uses a recall-based experiment with 220 hotel employees to establish causality. Study 2 draws on a two-wave field survey of 298 employees from five hotels in China to enhance ecological validity and test the boundary conditions. Findings The findings reveal that time poverty significantly undermines hotel employees’ proactive service behavior, thereby establishing the mediating role of future self-continuity. Furthermore, competitive climate moderates this effect such that the indirect negative effect becomes stronger when competitive climate is high. Practical implications This study helps hotel managers understand the impact of time poverty on employees and offers practical guidance for monitoring and alleviating it through employee-centered scheduling, workload redistribution and protected time, thereby sustaining employees’ proactive service behavior. Originality/value This study examines hospitality employees’ time poverty by shifting attention from the tourists’ temporal experiences, which have dominated prior research, to employees’ chronic scarcity. Moving beyond…

title: From bad to worse: customer mistreatment and service sabotage across encounters
abstract: Purpose Customer mistreatment is a significant issue in both practical and academic contexts, especially in the service industry. Drawing on the stressor–emotion model, this study aims to use a sequential two-encounter field design to test the lagged effects of customer mistreatment on service sabotage at Time 1 and Time 2. The study also explores the moderating effects of personal controls (i.e. conscientiousness and emotional stability) and situational control (empowerment) on the above relationships. Design/methodology/approach The analytical sample consisted of 190 frontline employees matched with 380 customer evaluations across two consecutive service encounters. Data were gathered in multiple stages: frontline employees first completed questionnaires on demographics and personal traits, and then, immediately after service encounters. This procedure was repeated for a subsequent service encounter with a second customer to capture multiple interactions for each employee. Findings The findings indicate that emotional exhaustion mediates the relationship between customer mistreatment and service sabotage at both Time 1 and Time 2. Furthermore, empowerment weakens the positive relationship between customer mistreatment and emotional exhaustion, whereas conscientiousness and emotional stability attenuate the indirect effect of customer mistreatment on service sabotage through e…

title: The Impact of Customs and Tariff Regulation on the Competitiveness of Export Oriented Industries
abstract: This article analyzes the impact of customs tariff regulations on the competitiveness of export-oriented Russian industries from 2016 to the first half of 2026. It shows that the raw materials bias in exports persists but is gradually weakening: while mineral products accounted for approximately 61% of export value in 2024, their share fell to 53.9% in 2025, amid significant growth in non-resource products such as metals, chemicals, and machinery. Non-resource, non-energy exports, which set a record in 2021, declined in 2023–2024 and recovered in 2025, confirming the indicator’s sensitivity not only to tariffs but also to sanctions, logistics, and global price conditions. The role of tariff escalation and flexible export duties — the grain damper, in effect since June 2021 and at zero for most positions in the summer of 2026 due to low world prices — is examined, together with the temporary zeroing of import duties on critical imports under the package of 2022 EEC Council decisions. Directions for further finetuning tariff policy in favor of highly processed products are identified.

title: Emotional-Level Happiness Management (ELHM) for Maternal Emotional Regulation: A Methodological Framework with Implications for Parent–Child Interaction and the Family Emotional Environment
abstract: Maternal emotional regulation is a central process in everyday family life. It shapes how a mother notices a child’s signals, responds under pressure, communicates limits, and restores connection after conflict. This methodological paper presents and operationalizes Emotional-Level Happiness Management (ELHM) as a coaching-based framework for maternal emotional regulation. The framework was developed through structured integration of the full ELHM architecture with a targeted synthesis of research on parenting stress, parental emotion regulation, family emotion socialization, positive psychology, and coaching. The maternal adaptation includes the KIT Reflective Assessment, the Seven Levels of Feelings, four core facilitation protocols, and a five-session individual format lasting 60–90 minutes per session. Its proposed mechanism connects emotional awareness, reduced automatic reactivity, resource-state formation, and integration with calmer communication, clearer boundaries, relational repair, and a more stable family emotional environment. The protocol specifies delivery conditions, session tasks, between-session practices, tailoring principles, and professional referral boundaries. By translating the ELHM method into a transparent maternal application, the article provides a replicable structure for coaching and educational practice and a defined platform for subsequent imple…

title: Field FBG monitoring of helicopter landing gear: data integrity screening and time–frequency characterization of operational events
abstract: Operational monitoring of helicopter landing gear can benefit from direct strain measurements able to resolve transient contact and roll-out dynamics. This work presents a field demonstration of a fiber Bragg grating (FBG) measurement and processing workflow applied to the main landing gear of an Erickson S-64 Skycrane operated by the Italian National Fire Brigade. Four gratings were bonded to the landing-gear structure, and wavelength data were acquired at 1 kHz during operational activities. The study does not aim to perform damage detection, health-state assessment, or hard-landing classification; rather, it evaluates whether field-acquired FBG signals affected by realistic acquisition imperfections can be transformed into interpretable time–frequency descriptors. Raw wavelength records were screened for dropouts, saturation artifacts, and spikes, then converted to normalized strain and high-pass filtered. Event-centered analyses based on Hann-window short-time Fourier transform (STFT), Thomson multitaper estimates, and ridge tracking revealed recurrent transient signatures and sensor-dependent frequency families in two representative datasets. The results support FBG-derived landing-event characterization under field conditions, while showing that synchronized avionics references, temperature compensation, and larger repeated datasets are required before validated Health an…

title: AI-driven knowledge transfer for cross-border data flow regulation and global cooperation: multi-dimensional considerations of privacy, compliance and efficiency
abstract: Purpose This study investigates artificial intelligence (AI)-driven knowledge transfer as a transformative catalyst for optimizing cross-border data flow regulation and advancing inclusive global cooperation, explicitly addressing the multi-dimensional equilibrium of privacy preservation, regulatory compliance and operational efficiency across diverse jurisdictions. Design/methodology/approach Based on the theory of knowledge capital, this study conceptualizes AI-driven knowledge transfer as a systematic migration and reconstruction process of knowledge capital in the cross-border regulatory field. This study employs a combination of quantitative regression analysis and multiple case studies, using regulatory datasets from the EU, China and the United States, to empirically examine the impact of AI-driven knowledge transfer on the efficiency, privacy protection and compliance of cross-border data flows. This approach empirically validates three core hypotheses regarding AI's capacity to enhance regulatory agility, fortify privacy safeguards through intelligent anonymization and sustain flow efficiency within compliance frameworks. Findings Empirical results confirm AI-driven knowledge transfer significantly elevates regulatory efficiency (e-commerce flow efficiency: 0.87), reduces privacy leakage risks and mitigates cross-jurisdictional friction via cooperative frameworks (stan…

title: Trends and Prospects for Improving the Legal Regulation of Digital Technologies in Customs Affairs in the Context of Globalization
abstract: The article examines the issues of legal support for the digitalization of customs administration. The impact of blockchain and artificial intelligence technologies on the efficiency of customs control is analyzed. Gaps in legislation regarding legal liability when using automated decision-making systems are identified. The necessity of systematizing the regulatory framework through the adoption of a specialized codified act — the Digital Code, designed to eliminate the fragmentation of legal regulation, is substantiated.

title: Existential Concerns, Emotional Regulation and Meaning in Life among Young Adults
abstract: The present study examined the relationships among existential concerns, emotional regulation and meaning in life among young adults. A quantitative, cross-sectional and correlational research design was used. The sample consisted of 250 young adults (121 males and 129 females) aged 18-25 years, selected through purposive sampling from colleges, universities and the local community in Lahore. Data were collected using the Existential Concerns Questionnaire (ECQ), Emotion Regulation Questionnaire (ERQ) and Meaning in Life Questionnaire (MLQ). Data were analyzed using SPSS. The findings indicated significant relationships among existential concerns, emotional regulation and meaning in life. Existential concerns were significantly negatively associated with the presence of meaning in life, indicating that greater existential concerns were related to a weaker sense of meaning. Cognitive reappraisal was significantly positively associated with meaning in life, suggesting that the use of adaptive emotion regulation was related to greater meaning in life. Contrary to the proposed hypothesis, expressive suppression showed a significant positive association with meaning in life. Overall, the findings suggest that existential concerns and emotional regulation are important factors associated with meaning in life during young adulthood. The unexpected positive relationship between express…

The Use of Videoconferencing in the Conduct of Investigative Actions: Legal Regulation, Possibilities and Prospects
abstract: This article examines current issues in the procedural regulation of investigative actions using videoconferencing. From both scientific and practical perspectives, the legislator’s intention to legitimize the remote format for certain investigative actions is positively assessed. It also recognizes the need to effectively adapt legislative regulation of the use of videoconferencing technology in pre-trial proceedings, taking into account current trends in the digitalization of criminal proceedings. The article also formulates proposals for revising controversial provisions of the criminal procedure law.

Music listening patterns and their associations with mood regulation, emotional processing, and cognitive performance: an intensive longitudinal questionnaire study
abstract: Background Music is often played when university students are studying and during their daily activities, but most of the research to date in the field of music listening and academic performance has used self-report techniques. Implications for student wellbeing and academic success are summarized where listening patterns are used to understand mood regulation and academic cognitive performance in real-world settings. Method The design of this study was intensive longitudinal (IL) using experience sampling methodology (ESM) with event-contingent sampling over the 14-day period. Hundred and twenty-eight university students filled out questionnaires that measured musical sophistication, alexithymia, personality and trait mood regulation at baseline, and then answered short questions on 5,448 music listening episodes. Within-person and between-person associations in relation to academic versus non-academic contexts were examined using multilevel modeling. Results Using music for mood regulation was the strongest predictor of mood improvement ( β = 0.87, p < 0.001), followed by active enjoyment ( β = 0.54, p < 0.001), while focus purposes predicted perceived academic cognitive performance ( β = 0.56, p < 0.001). Musical sophistication moderated the mood regulation-mood change relationship ( β = 0.22, p = 0.006), while alexithymia reduced its effectiveness ( β = −0.19, p =…

title: High-frequency observations of the variations of pCO2 in the Bohai Sea
abstract: The Bohai Sea, a semi-enclosed marginal sea under intense anthropogenic pressure, represents a critical yet dynamic component of the regional carbon cycle. However, understanding its fine-scale carbon dynamics has been limited by a lack of long-term, high-frequency observations. This study deployed a moored buoy system in the central Bohai Sea from September 2020 to December 2021 to obtain continuous, high-temporal-resolution measurements of surface seawater p CO 2 and key ancillary environmental parameters. An annual stepwise linear regression model (R 2 = 0.793, p< 0.001) revealed that p CO 2 variability is governed by a balance between biological drawdown (chlorophyll-a concentration, 16.76% relative contribution) and thermal forcing (SST, 27.69%). Seasonal sub-regressions demonstrated a systematic transition: biological control prevailed in autumn and summer (R 2 = 0.922), physical control dominated in winter (R 2 = 0.787), and spring exhibited low predictability (R 2 = 0.318), implicating unmeasured processes such as vertical mixing. An event-scale composite analysis of eight independent storm events identified a distinct two-phase p CO 2 response: an initial decline at the wind peak (from 354.7 to 333.7 μatm) due to enhanced solubility, followed by a delayed rise peaking four days later (355.8 μatm, net increase of 22.1 μatm), concurrent with SST cooling (2.62 °C) and …

Investigating the roles of experiential avoidance, emotion regulation difficulties and preoccupation with figure and weight in the relationship between post-traumatic stress and disordered eating in a sample of trauma-exposed women
abstract: Abstract Background This study aimed to test a cross-sectional model investigating the indirect association of experiential avoidance, emotion regulation difficulties, and preoccupation with figure and weight in the relationship between posttraumatic stress symptoms (PTSS) and disordered eating (DE) behaviors in a trauma-exposed sample. Methods Participants were 373 women aged between 18 and 58 who reported at least one traumatic event. Data were collected online via the Posttraumatic Diagnostic Scale for DSM-5 (PDS-5), Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale (DERS), Acceptance and Action Scale-2 (AAS-2), Munich Eating and Feeding Disorder Questionnaire, and Eating Attitude Test-26 (EAT-26) scales. To test the study’s proposed model, cross-sectional path analysis was conducted in AMOS. Results The findings indicated that without experiential avoidance and emotion regulation difficulties, the pathway of preoccupation with figure and weight was not significant between PTSS and EDs. However, the indirect paths including experiential avoidance and emotion regulation difficulties were significant both in the presence and absence of the preoccupation with figure and weight pathway. Furthermore, increases in experiential avoidance and emotion regulation difficulties were linked to higher levels of binge eating, vomiting, inappropriate compensatory behaviors, and preoccupation with fi…

title: The effect of optimism, pessimism, and jealousy on emotional regulation in athletes
abstract: Introduction The aim of this study was to examine the distinct associations of optimism and pessimism with emotion regulation in athletes and to test whether jealousy mediates each association. Methods The sample comprised 628 athletes from the Ataşehir and Bakırköy districts of Istanbul (mean age = 25.73). Data were collected using the Athlete Emotion Regulation Scale (AERS), the Athlete Optimism and Pessimism Scale (AOPS), and the Jealousy Scale for Athletes (JSA). Because AOPS is a two-factor instrument, optimism and pessimism were treated as separate subscale scores rather than combined into a single predictor. Two parallel mediation analyses were specified with Hayes PROCESS Model 4, with optimism or pessimism as the predictor (X), jealousy as the mediator (M), and emotion regulation as the outcome (Y). Results In the optimism model, optimism negatively predicted jealousy (B = −0.52, p < 0.001) and positively predicted emotion regulation after controlling for jealousy (B = 2.20, p < 0.001); the indirect effect through jealousy was negative and significant (B = −0.70, bootstrap 95% CI [−0.8232, −0.5982]). In the pessimism model, pessimism positively predicted jealousy (B = 1.50, p < 0.001) and showed a negative direct association with emotion regulation (B = −2.06, p < 0.001); the indirect effect through jealousy was approximately B = 5.27 and was reported as si…

title: Salivary cortisol reactivity to the Trier Social Stress Test-Online in habitual smokers: response blunting and recovery
abstract: Abstract Background In Japan, alcohol, tobacco, coffee, and tea are categorized as “ Shikohin ” (i.e., non-nutritious items consumed for flavor). Shikohin provides a culturally grounded lens for examining health-related behaviors like smoking. Using it as a framework, I hypothesized that participants with high resilience and strong smoking habits would show blunted cortisol responses to the Trier Social Stress Test-Online (TSST-OL). Based on a previous study showing that individuals with high alcohol consumption and high resilience scores exhibited a specific blunted cortisol response, the purpose is to examine whether a similar relationship can be detected in smoking habits, which are also categorized as Shikohin . Methods Participants ( N = 41) were classified into four groups based on the degree of smoking (≤ 14 or ≥ 15 cigarettes per day) and the median total score on resilience scales (low-resilience low-smoking, low-resilience high-smoking, high-resilience low-smoking, and high-resilience high-smoking). Participants completed the TSST-OL, measuring subjective stress and salivary cortisol, at eight time points. Exploratorily, a two-piece multilevel growth curve model with landmark registration (GCM-LR) examined the effects of smoking habits and resilience scores on cortisol concentrations. Results Both the Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) and the GCM-LR showed blunted cortisol…

Time-dependent transcriptomic response to scrapie exposure in ovine MSC-derived neuron-like cells
abstract: Prion diseases are fatal neurodegenerative disorders in which early molecular responses to prion exposure remain incompletely understood, particularly in naturally susceptible hosts. In the present study, we performed RNA-sequencing analysis of ovine mesenchymal stem cell-derived neuron-like cells exposed to classical scrapie brain homogenate and compared their transcriptomic response with that of cells exposed to normal brain homogenate. Cells were analyzed at 2 and 4 days post-inoculation (dpi). Differential expression analysis identified 76 genes at 2 dpi and 124 genes at 4 dpi, with limited overlap between time points, indicating a dynamic response to scrapie exposure. At 2 dpi, enriched biological processes among upregulated genes were mainly related to signaling- and immune-associated transcriptional responses, whereas downregulated genes were enriched in developmental, morphogenetic and lipid-related processes. At 4 dpi, the transcriptional profile was dominated by broader gene repression and showed reduced functional specificity. RT-qPCR analysis of eight selected genes supported the direction of change detected by RNA-seq in most cases. Overall, these results indicate that scrapie exposure elicits a time-dependent transcriptional response in ovine MSC-derived neuron-like cells and provide an exploratory framework for studying early molecular responses associated with p…

title: Anticipating user desires: predicting software product feature demand through consumer behavioral analytics
abstract: In this study, we introduce the Dynamic Behavioral Feature Predictor (DBFP), a machine learning model designed to predict feature demands for software products based on consumer behavioral analytics. The model leverages advanced techniques such as Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (1D CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to identify complex user behavior patterns. We demonstrate that DBFP achieves a high accuracy of 99%, outperforming established models such as LSTM and 1D CNN in extensive comparative experiments. Although the model shows promising performance, we note that its accuracy may be sensitive to data quality, and further research is needed to evaluate its robustness in real-world applications. DBFP excels at identifying diverse user behavior types, offering tailored recommendations for software features that align with individual user preferences. This paper highlights the potential of behavioral analytics in personalizing software development, enhancing the user experience, and improving the efficiency of feature prioritization. By bridging the fields of machine learning, big data (BD), and software personalization, DBFP lays the foundation for future advancements in user-centric software engineering. This study not only contributes to the field of predictive analytics but also opens new avenues for applying behavioral insights to software design and dev…

title: Tailoring Wood Shrinkage via Solvent-Driven Interfacial Engineering for On-Demand Applications
abstract: Abstract Modulating wood cell shrinkage offers a promising yet underexplored route to advanced timber-based materials. Here, we combine chemical softening with solvent evaporation-induced assembly for programmable shrinkage control. Solvent prewetting facilitates penetration of aqueous NaOH/Na2SO3/AQ, promoting cell-wall softening through partial removal of lignin and hemicellulose at elevated temperatures. Subsequent evaporation generates capillary stresses dependent on solvent surface tension, driving cellular shrinkage. Finite element simulations capture the macroscopic relationship between solvent surface tension and shrinkage, providing a mechanistic basis for tailoring the final thickness and mechanical stiffness. Extensive shrinkage produces a cellulose-rich lamellar structure with a tensile strength of 400.4 MPa and Young’s modulus of 24.6 GPa, approximately 20 and 10 times those of natural wood, respectively. Partial shrinkage nearly doubles volumetric capacitance while preserving ion-transport pathways. These results demonstrate that chemical softening and evaporation-induced reconstruction enable programmable structural and functional properties in wood.

title: Linking the triglyceride-glucose index to major adverse cardiocerebrovascular events in individuals with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: insights from an aggregate-data systematic review and dose–response meta-analysis
abstract: Background Epidemiological research has indicated a potential association between the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and the risk of major adverse cardiocerebrovascular events (MACCE). Nevertheless, the precise nature and magnitude of this relationship remain to be fully elucidated. Objectives This study aims to assess the dose–response relationship between the TyG index and MACCE among individuals with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome. Methods A comprehensive literature search was conducted using the PubMed and Web of Science databases to identify relevant studies on the TyG-MACCE relationship up to 16 June 2026. Data were synthesized using both random- and fixed-effects models, and nonlinear dose–response meta-analyses were performed using restricted cubic spline models. Results The analysis incorporated eight cohort studies, encompassing over two million participants and 179 thousand MACCE cases. The aggregated risk estimate for MACCE, comparing the highest to the lowest categories of TyG index exposure, was 1.20 (95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.11–1.30, I 2 = 77.2%, p heterogeneity < 0.001). The dose–response analysis revealed a nonlinear positive association between the TyG index and MACCE risk ( p nonlinear < 0.001), with summary risk estimates calculated for each 1-unit increment in the TyG index being 1.05 (95% CI = 1.02–1.08, I 2 = 81.1%, p heter…

title: Hepatoprotective action of Dendrobium officinale polysaccharide against MAFLD: modulation of gut microbiota-metabolite cascade controls TLR4/NF-κB inflammatory response
abstract: Introduction Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) threatens public health worldwide, and Dendrobium officinale polysaccharide (DOP) exhibits promising hepatoprotective potential, yet its regulatory mechanism targeting the gut microbiota-metabolite-TLR4/NF-κB inflammatory axis remains poorly defined. Methods In this study, in-vivo rat and in-vitro HepG2 cell MAFLD models were established. Male Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats received 12-week high-fat diet (HFD) feeding to induce MAFLD; HepG2 cells were exposed to a 1 mmol/L free fatty acid (FFA) mixture (oleic acid/palmitic acid = 2:1) for 24 h to trigger cellular steatosis. Serum, hepatic and cellular biochemical indexes, intestinal permeability factors and inflammatory mediators were detected. Hepatic pathological lesions and lipid accumulation were evaluated via hematoxylin-eosin (HE) and Oil Red O staining. Fecal metagenomics and untargeted metabolomics were applied to profile gut microbes and differential metabolites. RT-qPCR and Western blotting were used to assess tight-junction protein expression and TLR4/NF-κB pathway activation. Results DOP markedly alleviated hepatic lipid accumulation, restored liver function abnormalities and mitigated hepatic pathological damage. DOP reshaped the disturbed gut flora: it reduced lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-enriched Gram-negative bacteria, elevated short-chain fatty aci…

title: PREDICT-AML: personalized response via drug interaction with cellular traits for acute myeloid leukemia
Integrative multi-omics characterization of KLRB1/CD161 in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma: associations with immune context, subtype biology, and therapeutic response
abstract: Background The tumor immune microenvironment (TME) of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) displays pronounced heterogeneity, and existing immunotherapeutic approaches achieve only suboptimal outcomes for a considerable proportion of affected individuals. CD161—a C-type lectin receptor whose coding gene is KLRB1—has lately emerged as a modulator of T-cell activity in several malignancies; nonetheless, a thorough characterization of its function in DLBCL has not yet been undertaken. Methods Transcriptomic analyses quantified KLRB1 mRNA, whereas flow cytometry and immunoblotting assessed its encoded surface protein, CD161. Transcriptomic, genomic, epigenomic (methylation), and exploratory single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets from DLBCL cohorts were integrated with in vitro functional assays to characterize clinical associations, immune context, and hypothesis-generating therapeutic relationships. Results Pan-cancer analysis revealed predominantly inverse associations between KLRB1 mRNA and immunomodulatory features, whereas DLBCL bulk-tumor analyses showed positive correlations with MHC molecules, immune-cell infiltration estimates, CD8 + T-cell effector programs, and immune-checkpoint transcripts. KLRB1 mRNA was higher in ABC than in GCB DLBCL and was associated with vital status at last follow-up and clinical stage. Lower TIDE scores and pharmacogenomic modeling suggested explo…

title: Aberration-guided intraocular lens power calculation in keratoconus: ray-tracing optimization
abstract: Purpose: To evaluate the accuracy of ray-tracing optimization (RTO) for predicting postoperative refractive error in keratoconic cataract eyes. Setting: University Eye Clinic, Maastricht, the Netherlands. Design: Case series. Evaluation of technology. Methods: 22 keratoconic eyes that underwent cataract surgery were included in the study. Anterior and posterior corneal Zernike coefficients, axial distances, and intraocular lens (IOL) geometry were exported to custom-developed RTO algorithms to build patient-specific eye models. Optical quality was quantified with the Visual Strehl of the Optical Transfer Function (VSOTF) ratio. The defocus and astigmatism maximizing VSOTF were taken as the optimal target refraction and compared with postoperative subjective refraction using power vectors (spherical equivalent [SEQ], J 0 , and J 45 ). Agreement was assessed with Bland-Altman analysis, and prediction accuracy was summarized as the percentage within ±0.5 diopters (D) and ±1.0 D. Results: Bland-Altman analysis showed good agreement between RTO-predicted and postoperative subjective refractions, particularly for SEQ and J 0 (with-the-rule/against-the-rule astigmatism). The percentage of eyes within ±0.5 D of prediction error was 68.2% for SEQ and J 0 and 59.1% for J 45 ; within ±1.0 D, it was 86.3% (SEQ), 81.8% (J 0 ), and 77.3% (J 45 ). Cataract surgery in keratoconic eyes did not …

title: Ecosystem Resilience and Land-Use Governance: Remote Sensing Insights for Environmental Management in a Tropical Dry Forest
abstract: Abstract Seasonally Dry Tropical Forests (SDTFs), such as the Brazilian Caatinga, are highly vulnerable to climate change and chronic anthropogenic disturbances. Despite extensive land-use conversion, understanding how vegetation productivity and resilience vary across different land governance regimes remains a critical gap. Here, we integrated two decades (2004–2024) of remote sensing data to evaluate Net Primary Productivity (NPP) and Water Use Efficiency (WUE). We applied interannual climate anomaly analyses (Z-scores) and adapted a trend-based classification framework to assess ecosystem trajectories. These biophysical metrics were cross-referenced with the spatial boundaries of Conservation Units, Indigenous Lands, Quilombola Territories, and private properties, including a distance-decay edge effect analysis. While long-term temporal trends for NPP and WUE remained relatively stable over the two decades, standardized anomaly analyses revealed a strong, statistically significant inverse coupling between productivity and water-use efficiency ( r = − 0.741, p < 0.001), primarily mediated by surface moisture retention (LSWI) rather than immediate precipitation alone. Spatial analyses demonstrated that Conservation Units act as the main ecological refugia, maintaining peak restoration within a 0–2 km internal buffer. Notably, Indigenous Lands and Quilombola Territories exhibi…

USER-CENTRED INTERFACE DESIGN FOR AN AUGMENTED REALITY INFORMATION SYSTEM AT LEMBANG PARK & ZOO
abstract: Lembang Park & Zoo serves as both a wildlife conservation facility and an educational tourism destination. To support visitor education, the zoo currently utilizes digital and printed informational media. However, printed media present sustainability challenges due to paper consumption and waste generation, while also limiting the flexibility of information delivery. Augmented reality (AR) offers the potential to provide a more sustainable and interactive digital information medium, although its effectiveness depends on the design of an intuitive and user-centred interface. Therefore, this study aims to design a user interface for an AR-based information system at Lembang Park & Zoo based on visitors' needs and interaction preferences. This study employed a qualitative research approach through field observations and semi-structured interviews with zoo visitors to identify user requirements, information needs, and interaction patterns. The collected data were analysed descriptively to identify key themes that informed the interface design process. The findings indicate that visitors require a simple, intuitive, and visually engaging interface with clear navigation and contextual information that can be easily accessed during their visit. These findings were translated into user interface design recommendations for an AR application intended to support digital information delive…
